findings: No browser versus Node record difference or additional backend mapping difference was observed for linear and interrupt/resume.
Unflushed abrupt close lost all three pending spans in the sampled window; navigation with default auto flush and explicit flush each delivered all three to both backends.
Both verbatim guide scratch package sets exported a single SDK span despite API peer warnings; no second API version was installed. The latest web/base tags were deprecated.
The pinned live SDK uses an options-object processor constructor and manual API/context registration; the guide web SDK constructor and register() work in the scratch sets.

A short experiment identifier collided with the standardized Chromium navigation preference bit. A failing regression preceded the scanner correction; secret/canary scans still cover that header and arbitrary identifier headers still fail.
Lifecycle callbacks relayed during document destruction are incomplete observations; only backend span counts define the close measurements.
The preview receiver observed a keepalive export during navigation that Playwright did not report; full receiver headers and body bytes were also scanned.
